The present revision under Sections 397/401 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the revisionist- Rajendra Singh against the judgement and order dated 23.03.2018 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 1, Etah in Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2014 (Rajendra Singh Vs. State of U.P. and another) by which the said appeal has been dismissed, the judgement and order of the trial court has been affirmed and further against the judgement & order dated 03.09.2014 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 17, Etah in Case No. 689 of 2005 (State of U.P.
Vs. Rajendra Singh) under section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, P.S. Sakrauli, District Etah by which the accused / revisionist has been convicted & sentenced for offence under section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act to 06 months rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default of payment of fine to further undergo 01 month simple imprisonment.

sentences.text: 5. The case of the prosecution in brief is that on 21.12.2002 at about 12 p.m. Food Inspector Dev Raj Singh saw the revisionist displaying buffalo milk for sale near a school in Borikalan.
He then during his checking purchased 750 ml of milk and sealed it as per the rules for being sent to the food analyst for inspection.
The material was inspected by the food analyst and his report dated 02.02.2003 stated that milk fat is deficient by 7% and milk solids not fat is also deficient by 7%.

A complaint was filed after which notice u/s 13 (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was sent to the revisionist who exercised his option of getting the milk tested through Central Food Laboratory after which the material was sent to the Central Food Laboratory, Mysore who vide its report dated 17.06.2011 opined that the sample does not conform to the standards laid down for Buffalo Milk under the provision of PFA Act 1954 & Rules since milk fat was found to be 5.5%
whereas as per the standards it could not have been less than 6%.

The opinion as drawn is as follows:-
"Milk fat content falls below the minimum standard limit."
6. The trial started in which the statement of the complainant Dev Raj Sigh was recorded u/s 244 Cr.P.C. as P.W.-1.
There was no other witness produced u/s 244 Cr.P.C.
Subsequently u/s 246 Cr.P.C. the complainant Dev Raj Sigh, Food Inspector was produced and examined as P.W.-1.
Anil Kumar Bhardwaj the Food Clerk was examined as P.W.-2.

After completion of evidence of the said witnesses, the accused in his statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated in his additional submissions that he does not do the work of milk.
In his defence he produced Bhoori Singh the Village Pradhan as D.W.-1 and Narendra Pal Singh as D.W.-2.
The trial court disbelieving the testimonies of D.W.-1 and D.W.-2 produced by the accused in his defence and convicted the revisionist as stated above.
An appeal was preferred against the said judgement & order of conviction which stood dismissed and the judgement & order of the trial court was affirmed.

7. Learned counsel for the revisionist raised two arguments in the matter which are as under:-
(i) There is a difference in the report of the two analysts in as much as the report of the public analyst states of milk fat deficient by 7% and also milk solids not fat deficient by 7% but the Central Food Laboratory after its test quantified the milk fat to be present in the sample as 5.5% whereas as per the standards it could not have been less than 6% and had thus opined that milk fat contents was below the standard Rajendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192076732/
2 limit.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that there is a difference in the report of both the analysts with regards to contents of the milk fat and as such it would be unsafe to rely upon them to come to a conclusion that milk was adulterated.
(ii) The case of the revisionist-accused is that he does not do work of milk which is stated by him in his statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C.
The two defence witnesses produced by him also state of the same that he does not do work of milk and is a farmer having agricultural land.

The trial court has without cogent reasons disbelieved the said witnesses and the conclusion as dawn by the trial court is that since the witnesses are of the same village they are stating in favour of the revisionist-accused.

It is submitted that the said approach is not a legal approach and the testimony of the said defence witnesses stands unblemished which should have been given credence and accepted by the trial court.
8. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that looking to the said two arguments the present revision deserves to be allowed and conviction & sentence of the revisionist be set-aside.
9. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submitted that the trial court has returned cogent and well-found findings while convicting the revisionist.
It is submitted that the appellate court has also exercised its discretion on the basis of material available on record without any error apparent on the face of it.

10. After having heard the learned counsels for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the prosecution case as it stands is of the revisionist displaying milk for sale from which sample was taken and sent to the food analyst which was found to be adulterated.

A complaint was filed subsequent to which an option of getting the sample tested by the Central Food Laboratory was exercised by the revisionist and even before the Central Food Laboratory the sample was found to be adulterated.

In so far as the argument regarding difference in two reports of the laboratories is concerned, it is trite law that report of the Central Food Laboratory would prevail over the report of the food analyst.

11. In view of the same, the report of the Central Food Laboratory also opines the sample to be adulterated and as such the same would prevail over the report of the food analyst and the sample can be treated as adulterated.

12. The next argument regarding the revisionist not doing wok of milk is concerned and the evidence of two defence witnesses produced by the revisionist to substantiate the said case, the reading of the statement of said witnesses goes to show that D.W.-1 Bhoori Singh has stated that he is Village Pradhan of the village of revisionist.
He in categorical and specific terms states that revisionist does not do work of milk and he is a farmer having agricultural land.
D.W.-2 Narendra Pal Singh also in the same words states of the same.

The trial court disbelieving the said two witnesses has given its reasoning that since they are residents of the same village of the revisionist they would be taking side of the revisionist and as such are not truthful witnesses.
This reasoning does not stand good.
A witness in defence produced by the accused can be from anywhere.

In so far as D.W.-1 Bhoori Singh Rajendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192076732/
3 is concerned, he is a responsible person as has been Village Pradhan since the last two years.

entities.text: Bhoori Singh Rajendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has specifically stated of knowing the revisionist since the last 20 years.

Merely, for the reason that the defence witnesses are of the same village of the revisionist they cannot be held to be untrustworthy,
especially, if there is nothing concreted coming in their testimony in the cross-examination to show that they were brought up witnesses and due to any extraneous reason had given statement in favour of the accused.
The disbelieving of the said witnesses by the trial court is without any cogent reason.
The evidence of D.W.-1 & D.W.-2 coupled with the version of the accused in his statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C. goes to show that he does not do the work of milk.
13. The present revision is allowed.

The impugned judgement and order dated 23.03.2018 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 1, Etah and the impugned judgement and order dated dated 03.09.2014 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 17, Etah in the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.

The revisionist is on bail.
His bail bond is cancelled and sureties discharged.
15. Office is directed to transmit the copy of this judgement along with the trial court records to the concerned trial court forthwith for its compliance and necessary action.
16. The file be consigned to records.
